articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: Ernie Piini recounts his 12,000-mile journey to Australia in pursuit of a perfectly clear view of an annular 'Ring-of-Fire' solar eclipse, an experience he preferred despite past disappointments with cloud-obscured views. Accompanied by Joe Cali, he navigated travel logistics, explored cities like Perth and Geraldton, and visited Rottnest Island, all while seeking an ideal observation spot for the celestial event.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities calendar for April, May, and June, 1999. It details various star parties at multiple locations, general meetings with specific topics and speakers, observational astronomy classes, and mentions larger astronomical conferences like the Texas Star Party and Riverside Telescope Makers Conference.

articles.title: Continued from Page 1
articles.summary: This article details a successful observation of an annular solar eclipse east of Geraldton, Western Australia. The author describes the challenging environmental conditions, the equipment used, precise timings of the eclipse phases, and a significant temperature drop. The report concludes with a mention of a post-eclipse dinner attended by renowned eclipse chaser Fred Espenak, and some post-eclipse travel experiences.

articles.title: Continued from Previous Page
articles.summary: This article recounts a traveler's journey through Western Australia, detailing visits to natural wonders such as the red rock formations of Kalbarri National Park and the unique 'Pinnacles of the Desert'. The author emphasizes the incredible dark skies of the outback, offering breathtaking views of the Southern Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds. The narrative also includes observations on local wildlife, travel anecdotes, and a reference to a 'Ring-of-Fire' event, likely an annular solar eclipse.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article details an exceptional opportunity to observe a four-day-old crescent moon at sunset, made possible by its highest northerly declination. This alignment allows amateur astronomers to view typically hidden eastern limb features, such as Humbolt Sea and Mare Smythii, in a unique 'morning light' along the terminator. The piece highlights specific lunar features like Hercules, Atlas, Palus Somnii, and the Goclenius rilles for observation.

articles.title: Minutes of the Meeting of the SJAA Board of Directors
articles.summary: The SJAA Board of Directors met on March 27, 1999, where Dave North was elected President and Mike Koop as VP, though the Treasurer position remained open. Morris Jones filled an unexpired term, and the Observatory Committee was officially disbanded due to inactivity. A significant portion of the meeting was dedicated to discussing logistics and format changes for the upcoming Swap/Auction event, with some changes tabled for future discussion.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for May, primarily focusing on Mars, which is a week past opposition and making its closest approach to Earth. It offers tips for observing Mars, details specific features to look for, and includes reports from SJAA observers, emphasizing that even small telescopes can yield good views. Additionally, it covers the visibility and key events for other celestial objects like Venus, asteroids Ceres and Vesta, Pluto, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune, and a notable lunar occultation of Regulus.

articles.title: The Central Bulge — From Central Australia
articles.summary: This article details astronomical observations from Central Australia, specifically near Uluru (Ayers Rock), in April 1999. The author describes the region's geological history and the deep connection of Aboriginal culture to the night sky, including interpretations of celestial objects like the Magellanic Clouds and the Coal Sack. Key observations include detailed descriptions of the Large Magellanic Cloud, the Tarantula Nebula, Eta Carina, Omega Centauri, and the Milky Way, emphasizing the unique stargazing experience from this dark-sky location.

articles.title: Keep on Mooning
articles.summary: This article provides lunar observing tips for May 1999, highlighting opportunities to view features like Janssen crater and its rille system near the terminator. It also points out dates for strong northern limb libration, which allows for unique perspectives on edge-on craters and terraces. Additionally, it mentions the full Moon date and strong tides due to a close perigee.

articles.title: Meteor Watch
articles.summary: The article "Meteor Watch" by David North details two meteor showers active this month: the Eta Aquarids and the Sagittarids. It provides information on their activity periods, peak times, and visibility, noting the Eta Aquarids' origin from Halley's Comet and their better visibility from the Southern Hemisphere. The article also mentions the moon's influence on observing conditions for both showers, highlighting the Sagittarids' potential for fireballs.

articles.title: Yosemite Star Party
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has rescheduled its Yosemite Star Party at Glacier Point to July 30-31. This change, while coinciding with a significant moon phase, allows for the use of Bridalveil campground. Attendees are advised on telescope ratios and can sign up by contacting Jim Van Nuland.

articles.title: NCHALADA Meets
articles.summary: The Northern California Historical Astronomy Luncheon and Discussion Association (NCHALADA) held its 49th informal meeting on June 5, 1999, at Chabot Observatory in Oakland, California. The agenda included presentations on the "Prehistory and History of Calculus" led by Alan R. Fisher and "Lunar Probes" led by Nancy Cox, along with refreshments and lunch. NCHALADA operates without formal officers or dues, fostering multi-disciplinary discussions.

articles.title: Auction XIX
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) will host its "Auction XIX" on Saturday, April 24, at Houge Park in San Jose. This event, serving as SJAA's only fundraiser, includes an astronomical swap meet starting at noon and an auction beginning at 4 PM. Sellers will pay a 10% tax-deductible commission on sales, supporting the 403(c)(3) educational organization.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article, 'Comet Comments' by Don Machholz, provides updates on several comets, including Comet Linear (1998 T1 & 1998 M5), Comet SOHO (C/1999 C1), and Comet Li (1999 E1), detailing their visibility and discovery. It also includes 'Comet Hunting Notes,' analyzing the seasonal and hemispheric distribution of visual comet discoveries since 1975, noting trends in southern sky finds, even by Northern Hemisphere observers.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for two comets, C/1998 M5 (LINEAR) and C/1998 T1 (LINEAR). It lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation from the sun, and estimated sky magnitudes on a five-day interval from early April to early June. This data is essential for astronomers tracking and observing these specific comets.

articles.title: Elements
articles.summary: This document provides detailed orbital elements for two celestial objects named LINEAR (M5) and LINEAR (T1). For each object, parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude are listed, along with references to Minor Planet Center (MPC) citations. The document concludes with contact information for Don Machholz.

articles.title: Lunar Phases:
articles.summary: This document provides a schedule of key lunar phases, including Last Quarter, New Moon, First Quarter, and Full Moon. For each phase, it lists the date and time, along with associated rise, transit, and set times. This information serves as an ephemeris for tracking the moon's position and illumination.

articles.title: Nearer Planets:
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for the 'Nearer Planets' including Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. For three specific dates (the 7th, 17th, and 27th) within a given month, it details each planet's approximate distance from the Sun, apparent magnitude, and its rise, transit, and set times. Additionally, it lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), offering essential data for observers to locate and track these planets.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V
articles.summary: The article presents information about the Sun (SOL), identifying it as a G2V type star. It includes an ephemeris table detailing its rise, transit, and set times, along with its right ascension and declination for specific dates, adjusted for daylight saving. Additionally, it poses a question about intelligent life within the system.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight:
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing the start and end times for astronomical twilight across several specific Julian Dates. It provides precise timing information, likely intended as a reference for astronomers to plan observations during optimal dark sky conditions.

articles.title: Sidereal Time:
articles.summary: This document, an excerpt from the SJAA Ephemeris for May 1999, provides astronomical data including transit right ascension at local midnight for several dates in May. It also details the "Darkest Saturday Night" on May 15, 1999, listing sunset, twilight end, moonset, dawn begin, and total hours of darkness relevant for sky observation.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has announced that all its loaner telescopes are currently available for use by any SJAA member. Members wishing to borrow a scope are instructed to contact Mike Koop via email or phone to arrange the loan.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) maintains a list of telescopes available for immediate loan to its members. These scopes are stored at the homes of various SJAA members, and interested borrowers should contact Mike Koop to arrange pickup at an SJAA event.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: The document provides a list of telescopes currently on loan, detailing their descriptions, the borrowers, and their respective due dates. It also informs interested parties that they will be placed on a waiting list until a scope becomes available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists astronomical telescopes whose loan periods have been extended beyond their original terms. It provides details on how interested individuals can inquire about borrowing one of these currently loaned scopes by coordinating a transfer with the existing borrower. The list includes specific telescopes, their current borrowers, and either a due date or an 'Indefinite' status.

articles.title: Waiting List:
articles.summary: This document displays a waiting list, specifically listing one entry for a 'Solar Scope' currently borrowed by 'Bill Maney'. It appears to be a record tracking the allocation or availability of equipment.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors of an organization, including positions such as President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, and various Directors. It also details staff for specific programs like Ephemeris, Mentoring, Observational Astronomy, School Star Parties, and the Telescope Loaner Program, providing contact information for each role and individual.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The article encourages members to submit articles for the SJAA Ephemeris, the club's publication. Submissions should be sent to the editors via the provided email address, ephemeris@whiteoaks.com.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The 'SJAA Ephemeris' is identified as the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, published 12 times annually from January to December. The document also provides the association's postal address and details for subscribing or unsubscribing from their mailing list.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It outlines membership fees ($15 general, $6 junior) and an optional subscription to Sky & Telescope for an additional $27. The form provides instructions for submission via mail or in person, along with contact details for the organization.
